name: American Robin
habitat: Lawns, parks, forests, and backyards across Washington.
lifespan: Typically 2 years in the wild; the oldest recorded lived about 14 years.
funFact: Robins often tilt their heads as they listen for worms moving in the soil.

name: Bald Eagle
diet: Mostly fish, along with water birds and carrion.
habitat: Near lakes, rivers, and coastal waters, usually with tall trees for nesting.
lifespan: Can live around 20–30 years in the wild.
funFact: A pair may reuse and add to the same nest for many years.

name: Black-capped Chickadee
habitat: Woodlands, parks, and leafy neighborhoods throughout the state.
lifespan: Usually a few years in the wild; some live more than 10 years.
funFact: Its familiar “chick-a-dee-dee” call can include more “dee” notes when danger is greater.

name: Great Blue Heron
diet: Fish, frogs, small mammals, and other aquatic animals.
habitat: Wetlands, shorelines, rivers, and estuaries; it often nests in colonies.
lifespan: Often around 15 years in the wild, with some living longer.
funFact: It can stand almost motionless before striking quickly to catch prey.
